title: Disk SMART Health Monitoring
exclusions: Detects the newest successfully collected smartctl health verdict for directly visible ATA/SATA, SCSI/SAS, and NVMe devices. It does not predict every failure, prove data integrity, monitor filesystems or RAID redundancy, start self-tests, decode vendor-specific ATA raw attributes, apply one reallocated/pending-sector threshold to every model, or establish collection coverage when a device or host is silent. Drives hidden behind RAID controllers, USB bridges, virtual disks, multipath abstractions, or unsupported pass-through require separately qualified device arguments or vendor/BMC telemetry. Historical error-log and self-test-log bits are not alert criteria. The base SPL has no exception lookup and makes no compliance claim.
evidence: When deployed, retain the versioned `linux_disk_smart_health` saved-search definition and ACL, scheduler and triggered-alert history, result rows, matching normalized source events, the reviewed collector hash, effective `inputs.conf` and `props.conf`, `smartctl --scan-open` inventory output, same-time smartctl JSON used for validation, and dated positive/negative control results. These artifacts demonstrate the collector and rule behavior at recorded times only; they do not prove that every physical drive was visible, continuously polled, or free from latent failure.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a nonproduction `index=os` with `sourcetype=linux:smartctl:health`, index two recent, well-formed normalized JSON events on different device keys with `event_version=1`, `collector=smartctl_json_v1`, and `collector_status=ok`. Event A represents ATA: `host=smart-test-01`, `device=/dev/sda`, `device_key=ATA-TEST-01`, `device_protocol=ATA`, `smartctl_exit_status=16`, `smart_passed=1`, `attribute_threshold_failed=1`, and `nvme_critical_warning=null`. Event B represents NVMe: `host=smart-test-01`, `device=/dev/nvme0`, `device_key=NVME-TEST-01`, `device_protocol=NVMe`, `smartctl_exit_status=8`, `smart_passed=0`, `attribute_threshold_failed=0`, and `nvme_critical_warning=2`. Set valid `observed_at_epoch` values and search bounds that include both events. Expect exactly two rows: A with `health_reason="current ATA SMART attribute threshold failure"` and B with `health_reason="device-reported SMART health failure"`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: In the same isolated source type, index a healthy ATA event (`smartctl_exit_status=0`, `smart_passed=1`, `attribute_threshold_failed=0`) and a healthy NVMe event with those values plus `nvme_critical_warning=0`; expect no rows. Add an ATA event with only historical bit 5 set (`smartctl_exit_status=32`, `smart_passed=1`, `attribute_threshold_failed=0`) and expect no row because past threshold history is context, not a current failure. Finally add `collector_status=command_error` with `smart_passed=0`; it must still produce no health row because collector failures belong in the separate coverage alert.

dataSources: One compact normalized JSON event per discovered device per completed poll from a locally maintained smartmontools scripted input, routed to the deployment-selected `index=os` and local convention `sourcetype=linux:smartctl:health`. The collector uses `smartctl --scan-open --json`, then `smartctl --health --attributes --json --device <type> <device>` and emits only a stable contract rather than raw vendor attribute tables. Every event has `event_version, collector, collector_status, observed_at_epoch`; each successful per-device event also requires `device, device_key, device_type, device_protocol, smartctl_exit_status, smart_passed, attribute_threshold_failed`, with numeric `nvme_critical_warning` for NVMe and null otherwise. Scan-level coverage events cannot identify a device. Splunk supplies `_time, host, source, sourcetype`. `index=os`, the source type, app name, and normalized field names are local conventions, not smartmontools or Splunk_TA_nix fields.
app: A locally maintained `TA_linux_smartctl` deployment app containing the reviewed Python scripted input and matching JSON source-type configuration. A Splunk Universal Forwarder can execute and forward the events, but it is not a Splunkbase app and has no Splunkbase ID. smartmontools is an operating-system package prerequisite. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux is not required and does not define this collector contract.
spl:
index=os sourcetype="linux:smartctl:health" earliest=-40m@m latest=-5m@m
| spath
| eval observed_at_epoch=tonumber(observed_at_epoch), smartctl_exit_status=tonumber(smartctl_exit_status), smart_passed=tonumber(smart_passed), attribute_threshold_failed=tonumber(attribute_threshold_failed), nvme_critical_warning=tonumber(nvme_critical_warning)
| where event_version=1 AND collector="smartctl_json_v1" AND collector_status="ok" AND isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(device_key) AND isnotnull(device) AND observed_at_epoch>0 AND (smart_passed=0 OR attribute_threshold_failed=1 OR (isnotnull(nvme_critical_warning) AND nvme_critical_warning>0))
| sort 0 -_time
| dedup host device_key
| eval health_reason=case(smart_passed=0,"device-reported SMART health failure", attribute_threshold_failed=1,"current ATA SMART attribute threshold failure", nvme_critical_warning>0,"NVMe critical warning is nonzero")
| table _time host device device_key device_protocol model_name serial_number smartctl_exit_status smart_passed attribute_threshold_failed nvme_critical_warning health_reason
| sort 0 host device
description: Reports the newest failing row per host and stable device key from a closed 35-minute search interval when smartctl reports a failed health verdict, its current ATA prefailure-threshold bit is set, or an NVMe critical-warning value is nonzero. It preserves device identity, protocol, model, exit mask, normalized verdicts, and reason while excluding collector errors from health conclusions.
value: A drive-reported health failure or current standards-based warning can precede service loss or media unavailability. Routing that signal with exact device identity helps infrastructure teams protect redundancy, back up exposed data, and arrange replacement before a degraded disk becomes an avoidable outage, without creating false confidence from model-specific raw counters.
implementation: Deploy the reviewed `TA_linux_smartctl` collector only to Linux hosts with locally visible supported drives and smartmontools JSON output. Poll every 15 minutes, normalize smartctl's health verdict, current ATA threshold-failure bit, and NVMe critical warning into one JSON line per device, and route to the selected OS index. Validate discovery and fields against the same host's smartctl JSON, create a separate inventory-backed collection-health search, then schedule `linux_disk_smart_health` every 15 minutes and alert on any returned current failure row.
visualization: Use a current-health-failures table with host, stable device key, device path, protocol, model, health reason, warning value, and last observation; a fleet panel counting `collector_status` by host and status; and an inventory-backed freshness table for expected devices without an `ok` event inside two poll cycles. Add a drilldown to recent normalized events and separately qualified vendor or RAID telemetry. Do not render absent devices as healthy or label an ATA exit-bit finding as a universal sector count.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. Splunk CIM has no documented accelerated dataset for smartctl's device-health verdict, ATA SMART threshold state, or NVMe critical-warning bitmask. The source type and normalized fields are local, so an accelerated `tstats` equivalent would require a separately designed and validated data model rather than an invented CIM mapping.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row represents a real smartctl verdict or current threshold condition in the normalized event. "False positive" here means an expected test, an identity/collection defect, or a warning that local operations has already contained—not an invented disk fault.

1. **Approved smartmontools or storage qualification fixture** — A laboratory image, CI replay, or hardware acceptance test may deliberately emit a failed `smart_status` or exit bit. Match the exact nonproduction host, serial/device key, test job, fixture hash, and bounded execution window. Mute notification routing only for that test identity and retain the result as control evidence.

2. **Duplicate paths to one physical device** — Multipath, controller aliases, namespaces, or overlapping scan definitions can produce more than one device path for the same hardware. Compare serial number, WWN/NQN where available, controller topology, and `smartctl --scan-open` output. Correct discovery or derive an approved stable identity; do not suppress all alerts from one path until operators prove they are the same device.

3. **USB/SAT or RAID pass-through defect** — A bridge or controller can return incomplete, stale, or misleading SMART responses. smartctl documents that device type and pass-through matter. Compare a direct vendor/controller view, try only the documented `--device` form for that hardware in a maintenance window, and classify unsupported collection separately. Never convert a command failure into `smart_passed=1`.

4. **NVMe warning during an approved thermal or endurance test** — A controlled chamber, firmware, failover, or read-only transition test can intentionally set one or more critical-warning bits. Confirm the exact controller, warning mask, environmental reading, test plan, and end time. A nonzero warning remains a device finding; use a time-bound routing mute and verify it clears after the test.

5. **Known drive fault already drained and awaiting replacement** — Repeated polls continue reporting a legitimate failure after workloads have moved. Correlate the serial/device key with the incident, asset state, redundancy check, and replacement work order. Deduplicate in incident tooling while preserving every source event and re-page if the device identity, warning mask, host, or containment state changes.

6. **Path or serial identity changed after reboot or replacement** — `/dev/sdX` names are not stable, and some bridges omit or duplicate serials. Compare model, capacity, enclosure slot, WWN/NQN or controller inventory before joining history. Fix `device_key` generation for that hardware class rather than suppressing apparently duplicated rows.

**Safe suppression:** keep the catalogue SPL lookup-free. If local policy requires a mute, apply a governed wrapper lookup keyed by exact `host` and `device_key`, with `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `ticket`, `owner`, and `reason`. Reject wildcards, serial-only fleet exemptions, missing bounds, and permanent entries. Suppress notification actions—not source ingestion or retained base results—and review the entry when the warning mask or device identity changes.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational storage-device reliability monitoring; no adversary behavior is asserted)
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against smartmontools, NVM Express, and Splunk primary sources; collector and synthetic SPL contract not executed in a Splunk runtime or on physical drives; no storage SME sign-off
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement boundary

Assign a Linux/storage owner and a Splunk content owner. Install smartmontools on each in-scope Linux host and verify that the deployed build supports `--json` and `--scan-open`. Run discovery as the same operating-system account that will execute the scripted input; SMART access commonly requires root or narrowly delegated device permissions. Use the least privilege supported by the host and controller policy, and never make device nodes broadly writable. The collector requires a system Python 3 interpreter, not Splunk's private runtime. The forwarder service needs execute permission on the collector, permission to invoke smartctl, read access to in-scope device nodes, and its normal outbound forwarding path. The search owner needs access to the selected OS index plus permission to create scheduled searches and alert actions.

This use case relies on the verdicts smartctl derives from device protocols. For ATA, `smart_status.passed` is the overall SMART status and exit bit 4 means a current prefailure attribute is at or below its device threshold. For NVMe, smartmontools sets `smart_status.passed` false when the NVMe critical-warning value is nonzero and exposes that value in `smart_status.nvme.value`. NVM Express defines the critical warning as the principal health signal. The collector intentionally does not export or threshold ATA attribute IDs 5, 197, 198, CRC counts, wear names, or raw values: ATA attributes and raw encodings are vendor/model-specific, while NVMe defines a different standardized health log. The removed `reallocated_sectors>100` rule therefore had no defensible universal field contract or threshold.

`index=os`, `sourcetype=linux:smartctl:health`, `TA_linux_smartctl`, and every flattened field are explicit local conventions. Replace the index/source type in collection and SPL together if the deployment uses other names. The Universal Forwarder is a Splunk distribution, not Splunkbase app 617; no Splunkbase app is required. Splunk Cloud can receive the forwarded data but does not execute this host-local collector.

## 1. Configure and qualify the collector

Place the exact `scriptExample` at `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_linux_smartctl/bin/collect_smart_health.py`, owned by the forwarder administrator and executable only as required. It first requests `smartctl --scan-open --json`; for each discovered entry it preserves smartctl's detected `--device` type and runs `--health --attributes --json`. A nonzero process status is not automatically a collector failure because smartctl uses a bitmask for both command errors and health findings. Bits 0 through 2 cause `collector_status=command_error`; health bit 3 and current ATA threshold bit 4 remain searchable findings. Historical bit 5, error-log bit 6, and self-test-log bit 7 are retained only inside `smartctl_exit_status` and do not independently alert.

The script emits one compact, single-line JSON object per device. It normalizes only documented cross-device signals and basic identity, avoiding large smartctl payloads and vendor-specific raw-attribute assumptions. `collector_status=ok` requires a boolean health verdict, no command-error bits, and—for NVMe—a numeric critical-warning value. `scan_error`, `no_devices_discovered`, `invalid_json`, `command_error`, `smart_status_unavailable`, and `contract_incomplete` are coverage states; retain and alert on them separately instead of converting missing fields to healthy values.

Configure the input in the app's `local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://./bin/collect_smart_health.py]
disabled = 0
interval = 900
index = os
sourcetype = linux:smartctl:health
```

Splunk documents that an integer interval begins after the prior invocation completes. A 900-second setting is therefore approximately 15 minutes plus discovery/runtime, not exact wall-clock alignment. One poll emits one event per discovered device; at four polls per hour, ten devices normally produce about 960 compact events per host per day. Measure actual runtime and bytes. If one device command regularly approaches the script's 60-second timeout, qualify that controller separately rather than shortening the poll interval.

Use search-time JSON extraction and one-event-per-line parsing. On the required Splunk tiers, configure:

```ini
[linux:smartctl:health]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
TRUNCATE = 4096
DATETIME_CONFIG = CURRENT
KV_MODE = json
```

Do not also set `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON`; Splunk warns that combining indexed JSON extraction with `KV_MODE=json` duplicates fields. `DATETIME_CONFIG=CURRENT` makes `_time` the index-time observation; the explicit `observed_at_epoch` remains available to verify script completion. Inspect winning configuration with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` on the forwarder and `splunk btool props list linux:smartctl:health --debug` on applicable parsing/search tiers.

Before fleet deployment, compare `smartctl --scan-open` with the physical/server inventory. RAID controllers, HBAs, USB/SAT bridges, multipath, and NVMe namespaces can require model-specific pass-through or produce aliases. Put each qualified hardware class in a controlled deployment group and preserve its tested device arguments. Do not assume an empty scan means a diskless host, and do not modify the script to guess RAID slot syntax from vendor names.

## 2. Create and understand the health search

Save the catalogue SPL as `linux_disk_smart_health` and schedule it every 15 minutes, after expected forwarding latency. The embedded `earliest=-40m@m latest=-5m@m` selects a closed 35-minute interval that should contain roughly two polls while excluding the newest five minutes; increase the delay and move both bounds if measured p95 ingestion latency exceeds five minutes. Trigger when result count is greater than zero, route by host and device key to Linux/storage operations, and use incident-system deduplication rather than deleting repeated source rows.

`spath` parses the compact JSON even when source-type extraction is misconfigured, then numeric conversion prevents lexical comparisons. The contract filter requires event version 1, the named collector, host/device identity, a valid observation epoch, and `collector_status=ok`. The failure expression has three explicit branches: `smart_passed=0`; current ATA bit 4 normalized as `attribute_threshold_failed=1`; or any nonzero NVMe critical-warning integer. Zero is the only clear NVMe warning mask. There is no percentage, sector count, rate, or fleet baseline in this rule.

The descending time sort and `dedup host device_key` retain only the newest failing event for each device in the search interval. This means a later healthy event removes neither an earlier failing event before filtering nor an unresolved alert by itself—the current pipeline filters failures before deduplication. That behavior deliberately preserves a recent failure for investigation during the closed interval. Responders must inspect the newest source event and device state before closing. If local policy requires strictly current-state reporting, redesign the sequence to deduplicate all valid observations before the failure filter and update both controls; do not silently change semantics.

The `case` label reports the first matched reason, while all normalized values remain in the table for multiple simultaneous findings. `smart_passed=0` takes precedence because it is the device-level verdict. An ATA bit-4 row with a passing overall verdict is labeled as a current threshold failure. A consistent current smartmontools NVMe row with a nonzero warning also has `smart_passed=0`, so it receives the device-reported label and displays the warning mask for decoding in the runbook.

## 3. Validate discovery, normalization, and control logic

Run the collector manually as the forwarder service identity on a nonproduction representative of each hardware class. Confirm every stdout line is standalone valid JSON and stderr is empty. For each discovered drive, run the same `smartctl --health --attributes --json --device <type> <device>` command under that identity. Match device path/type/protocol, model, serial, `smart_status.passed`, `smartctl.exit_status`, and for NVMe `smart_status.nvme.value`. Confirm `attribute_threshold_failed` equals 1 only when protocol is ATA and exit bit 4 is set. Never clear a smartctl bit merely to make the event `ok`.

Validate field extraction with `index=os sourcetype=linux:smartctl:health earliest=-30m | spath | table _time host collector_status device device_key device_protocol smartctl_exit_status smart_passed attribute_threshold_failed nvme_critical_warning`. Check one line per discovered device per completed poll and compare `observed_at_epoch` with `_time` and `_indextime`. Investigate missing, duplicate, or delayed identities. Use an inventory lookup to find expected hosts/devices with no recent `ok` event; the primary health search cannot identify silence because absence creates no row.

Execute the exact positive and negative `controlTest` fixtures with fixed times inside the search bounds. Confirm two positive rows and exact reasons. Confirm healthy rows, historical bit 5 alone, and a command-error row do not appear. Also test bit 4 with `smart_passed=1`, the inclusive nonzero NVMe boundary with warning value 1, and malformed numeric strings; malformed events must not become health findings. Repeat after smartmontools, Python, script, controller firmware, forwarder, source-type, or SPL changes.

Do not induce a physical fault, overheat a drive, exhaust spare capacity, force read-only mode, or corrupt media to test this rule. Synthetic normalized events test SPL logic. Hardware laboratories may use vendor-approved fault injection under a written test plan, but must retain controller model/firmware, drive model/firmware/serial, exact command output, safety controls, source event, search job ID, and expected result. This editorial review does not claim that such a test or any Splunk runtime execution occurred.

## 4. Alert, visualize, respond, and preserve evidence

Build the three views described in `visualization`. The health table should drill down to all normalized events for the host/device key and to the separate collection-status/freshness view. Restrict serial numbers and topology to infrastructure roles because they are asset identifiers. Do not expose arbitrary smartctl execution through a dashboard token or alert action.

The runbook begins by identifying the exact physical device and confirming the latest collector status. Re-run a read-only smartctl health/attribute query with the qualified device type, inspect RAID/HBA/BMC or NVMe management telemetry where applicable, and check filesystem/volume/RAID redundancy plus current backups. For `smart_passed=0`, treat the device vendor's failing verdict as urgent. For ATA bit 4 with a passing overall status, inspect smartctl's named failed-now attribute and the drive vendor/OEM documentation; do not infer a universal raw count. For NVMe, decode the critical-warning mask against the applicable NVMe specification and OEM guidance. Engage the storage/hardware owner, protect exposed data, drain workloads if the redundancy and service runbook calls for it, and open a replacement case with the exact model, serial, firmware, and evidence.

The alert must not automatically start a self-test, clear a log, reset a controller, offline a path, fail a RAID member, remount a filesystem, reboot a host, or destroy data. Those actions can affect performance, redundancy, and recoverability and require platform-specific change control. Continue collecting after containment so the incident record shows whether the warning persisted or cleared.

Retain the artifacts named in `evidence` according to the operations and asset-data retention policy. Record the smartmontools package/version, JSON format version observed during qualification, collector hash, hardware class, threshold semantics, exception decision, incident, and final disposition. A retained passing event proves only the device returned a passing verdict at that observation; SMART cannot guarantee future reliability or detect every failure mode.

## 5. Monitor coverage and troubleshoot specific failures

Create a companion alert over all statuses, grouped by host and device, and compare successful device keys with authoritative hardware inventory. Page or ticket when an expected host has no event for two completed poll cycles, discovery returns no devices unexpectedly, any device remains outside `ok`, or the discovered device count changes without an approved inventory event. Keep this coverage rule separate: a collector error is not a disk-health failure, and a quiet health search is not evidence of collection.

- **`scan_error` or no script events** — Verify the app and executable path, the system Python shebang, smartctl path, service-account permissions, and `ExecProcessor` messages in `splunkd.log`. Splunk records scripted-input stderr there; the supplied collector emits bounded error detail to stdout for coverage events.
- **`no_devices_discovered`** — Run `smartctl --scan-open --json` as the service account and compare host inventory. The device may be virtual, hidden behind a controller, inaccessible, asleep, or unsupported. Qualify the correct vendor-documented pass-through; never interpret the empty list as healthy.
- **`command_error` with bits 0–2** — Decode the exit mask using the smartctl manual. Check command syntax, device open/identity, SMART command support, permissions, bridge/controller behavior, and checksums. Fix collection before assessing health from partial fields.
- **`smart_status_unavailable`** — The device/report did not provide a boolean `smart_status.passed`. Confirm `--health`, SMART support/enablement where applicable, device type, and current smartmontools behavior. Do not fallback to `health!="PASSED"`, because a missing string would become a false failure.
- **`contract_incomplete` on NVMe** — The report lacked numeric `smart_status.nvme.value` and the fallback health-log field. Compare raw JSON with the qualified smartmontools version and NVMe support. Upgrade or adapt the collector under review; do not synthesize zero.
- **Fields are null although raw JSON is valid** — Confirm `KV_MODE=json` reached the search tier, no competing props stanza disabled extraction, and events were not truncated. The primary SPL's `spath` should still parse a compact event; inspect `_raw` and effective props rather than renaming absent fields.
- **Duplicate device rows** — Check overlapping scripted stanzas, aliases, namespaces, multipath, repeated serials, and controller scan behavior. Remove duplicate collection or define a hardware-qualified stable key. `dedup` limits alert rows but does not repair inventory or licensing waste.
- **Device path changed but serial remained** — This is expected after some reboots or hot-plug operations; `device_key` joins by serial when supplied. Verify it is the same physical drive before carrying containment forward. If a bridge returns blank or duplicate serials, use an approved enclosure/controller identity strategy.
- **A failed row remains after a later healthy poll** — The base search intentionally reports any failure in the closed interval before deduplication. Inspect the newest raw event and incident history. If the warning flapped, retain both and investigate power, temperature, path, or firmware causes rather than immediately closing.
- **Long runtime or skipped cadence** — Smartctl discovery and per-device commands run serially with a 60-second timeout each, and Splunk starts the next interval after completion. Measure runtime by device count, investigate a slow controller, and split hardware classes or redesign concurrency only after testing output ordering and resource impact.
grandmaExplanation: We ask each storage drive whether it has raised its own serious health warning. If it has, the team can protect the data and arrange a replacement before the problem becomes a larger outage.
